newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher amid "bottomed out" talk.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher amid "bottomed out" talk.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher in active volumes amid signs that the market may have bottomed out, traders said.
"It looks like the EU and Argentine (wheat) prices may be bottoming out, and we may have some good export business coming in here in the next week," a KCBT trader said.

Traders said the gains made on fundamental news ushered in technical short covering. They said Refco's purchase of 1.7 million December bushels was the impetus behind a midsession rally that took the Dec contract as high as $4.27 a bushel, up 11 cents a bushel on the day.

But KCBT wheat values fell back from their highs and closed 2-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 7-1/2 at $4.23-1/2 a bushel. Monday's price action marked the December contract's fourth consecutive higher close.
The Dec/March spread traded as wide as 31 cents late after trading at 28-3/4 cents early. CIS was a key bull-spreader, buying 1.6 million bushels of the Dec/March spread from 28-3/4 to 31 cents.

General Mills bought 1.2 million March. Man International bought 1.3 million Dec and sold 900,000 March. Term Commodities sold 1.8 million March and Prudential Securities sold one million Dec bushels.
